newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian pipeline repairs due Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Colombian pipeline repairs due Wednesday.

text.p: Repair teams are scheduled to begin work on repairing Colombia's second largest oil pipeline Wednesday after it was blown up by leftist rebels, a spokesman for state-run oil company Ecopetrol said.
The 300,000 barrel per day capacity Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline was dynamited twice in less than four days last week.

No crude has been pumped for 10 days since the first blast and on Tuesday Occidental Petroleum Corp declared force majeure in the Cano Limon field because of "uncertainty" over how long the pipeline would remain out of action.
Ecopetrol also declared force majeure on the delivery of two crude shipments due to be dispatched from the Caribbean coast lifting terminal at Covenas earlier this week.

"We're programmed to go in and repair the pipeline today. The first rupture was repaired last Thursday but we still have to fix the second break which took place just an hour after the first was repaired," an Ecopetrol spokesman in northeast Norte de Santander province said.
In comments to reporters late Tuesday, Maj. Rafael Hernandez, commander of the army's Second Division, said troops had secured the area where the pipeline was attacked.
National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas killed 30 troops in two separate attacks last week as soldiers went to check out the blast sites.
Local media said the pipeline may have been blown up again Wednesday morning. Ecopetrol sources were unable to confirm the report.
